newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Petrovietnam submits new study for refinery.
newsitem.headline: Petrovietnam submits new study for refinery.

text.p: Vietnam's state oil and gas firm Petrovietnam said on Tuesday it had submitted for government approval a new feasibility study to build a refinery in the central province of Quang Ngai, a long-controversial location.

"The detailed feasibility (study) has been completed and has been submitted to the government at the end of March," said Ngo Duong Hung, Deputy Director of Petrovietnam's Oil and Gas Processing Department.

He said the study was carried out solely by Petrovietnam, which earlier this year rejected demands for further commercial and financial incentives from a consortium of foreign companies that had planned to take part in the project. Petrovietnam has said it is ready to build the $1.3 billion plant on its own.
The refinery, which Vietnam says it desperately needs by early next century to cut a growing bill for petroleum product imports, has long been a subject of controversy.
The consortium had been put together to replace France's Total, which walked away from the project in 1995 after deciding the location made it "economically unviable".

Petrovietnam has said that switching the proposed location from Dung Quat, an undeveloped area that is 1,000 km (600 miles) north of the country's oilfields and major consumption base, is out of the question.

The Saigon Times Daily last week quoted Petrovietnam President Ngo Thuong San as saying the project might be scaled down. However, it did not explain how original plans for the 6.5-million-tonne per year refinery may be adjusted.
Hung declined to give details of Petrovietnam's new feasibility study or specify whether it left the door open for foreign investors to join the project.

San told the Saigon Times last week that three members of the foreign consortium -- South Korea's LG Group LUGG.CN, Malaysia's state oil firm Petronas and U.S. refiner Conoco, a unit of DuPont Co. -- were determined to remain in the project.
